acceptance_rule: Correctness, originality, and value must all pass.

correctness.rationale: At a selected vertex, two selected neighbours in the same factor direction would have that vertex as the unique internal point of their length-two geodesic because girth at least five forbids both triangles and a second common neighbour. Hence the selected induced graph has degree at most two. Four consecutive vertices of a selected path/cycle must alternate factor directions; for endpoints separated by two forced steps in one factor and one edge in the other, every shortest shuffle passes through at least one of the two selected internal vertices. A Cartesian four-cycle fails similarly for opposite corners. Thus no connected mutual-visibility set has size four, while every three-vertex Cartesian corner works via the unused fourth corner. The centre is unique, and summing \(d_G(g)d_H(h)\) gives \(4|E(G)||E(H)|\). The definition-level verification script was inspected and correctly checks all small atlas factors, but the finite enumeration is only corroboration.
sources: current RESULT.md and verification script at archived record

broader_coverage.evidence: Ordinary product formulas can be much larger, e.g. grids, and the block theorem does not bound a 2-connected Cartesian product to three.
broader_coverage.reasoning: No checked broader theorem mechanically implies the sharp upper bound or maximizer classification.

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: That source fact gives only the lower observation that a nontrivial Cartesian product cannot have value two; it does not provide the upper bound three.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The alternating-direction geodesic obstruction and complete corner classification are additional structural work.
claim_vs_prior_implication.search: source theorem \(\mu_c(X)=2\) iff girth at least five plus product contains a four-cycle

equivalent_formulations.evidence: The introducing paper's abstract lists bounds, extremal characterizations, block locality, and complexity, with no product formula. Earlier product papers study the older ordinary parameter.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Connected mutual visibility is a distinct maximum parameter because the selected set must induce a connected graph.
equivalent_formulations.search: connected mutual visibility; Cartesian product; high girth; grids; Cartesian corners

originality.rationale: The paper introducing connected mutual visibility gives general structural, block, and complexity results but its public primary description does not state a Cartesian-product theorem. Earlier Cartesian-product literature concerns ordinary, total, lower, or related mutual-visibility parameters. published-result corpus searches for connected mutual visibility in high-girth Cartesian products returned this record as the first exact theorem; nearby rook/line-graph records are later or concern low-girth factors.
residual_risks: The invariant is extremely recent, so parallel unindexed work is a material residual originality risk.
The full arXiv body of the introducing paper was not retrievable, but its abstract and published-result corpus coverage checks did not reveal a product theorem.

source_inspections.assessment: Concerns ordinary mutual visibility, not the connected parameter.
No earlier exact/high-girth product theorem found.
source_inspections.material_read: semantic search for connected mutual-visibility products

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete, shape-independent product law, classifies every maximizer, and exhibits an unbounded separation from ordinary mutual visibility on grids. This is a natural exact theorem for a newly introduced graph invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice.
risks: The scope is restricted to high-girth factors and does not address the richer low-girth product regime.

final_claim: If \(G\) and \(H\) are connected finite nontrivial graphs of girth at least five, then \(\mu_c(G\square H)=3\); the maximum connected mutual-visibility sets are exactly the Cartesian corners, and there are \(4|E(G)||E(H)|\) of them.
limitations: The theorem treats exactly two factors and assumes both have girth at least five.
It does not classify mixed low-girth factors or higher Cartesian powers.
